item.title: Global Lacrosse Games roster breakdown: Australia women
item.description: Australia has historically battled for a top-four international ranking in every world tournament it’s been a part of. The teams that have stood in its way: the USA, Canada, England and the Haudenosaunee. Australia will have a chance to make its case against three of those four nations at the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games. Finding the perfect balance between veteran experience and young talent could be the recipe for Australia’s success in this tournament. As they prepare to take the field in Washington, D.C., in early December, let’s break down Australia’s roster. Field Players Grace Fujinaga Bec Lane Georgia Latch Ocea Leavy Erin Mitchell Hannah Nielsen Lauren Tolve Bonnie Yu Theadora Kwas Marlee Wood Miriam Suares-Jury Goalies Natalie Eastwood Elizabeth Hinkes One word to describe this roster is… Experienced. Hannah Nielsen’s 20-plus years of playing for Australia speak volumes. The lacrosse legend has played in international championship settings wearing the Australian uniform since the early 2000s. No one on any opposing team can match her experience, game-learned lessons and long-lasting national pride. The New York Charging’s Grace Fujinaga has been playing with programs in Melbourne, Australia, since 2023 and officially made her World Championship debut in Tokyo this past summer. She brings a wealth of high-level game experience from her college career at Penn and Northwestern, as well as at the professional level in the WLL. Marlee Wood is another intriguing name on this roster. Wood played with the U19 national team and on two World Championship rosters with Australia, earning silver in Prague in 2009 and bronze in Canada in 2013. She played collegiately at Loyola (‘14), and after stepping away from the sport for some time, she is making a comeback after having her second child in hopes of making the Australian team for the 2028 Olympics. Australia will need the wisdom and championship experience of these leaders to spearhead a successful Global Lacrosse Games. Biggest star: Georgia Latch What makes Latch such a dominating force is her innate ability to facilitate offense in multiple ways. Her stat lines throughout her career show a consistent balance across goals and assists. Without even watching her play, this tells us she is a dual threat with the ball. Her stickwork is out of this world, her decision-making with the ball is that of a champion, her power shots are noteworthy and her ability to make her teammates look good is superior. Latch has been a consistent standout for the Australian national team ever since she scored six goals in the bronze-medal game at the 2019 U19 World Lacrosse Championships. As a rising sophomore in college, she led the senior Australian team with 19 points in the 2022 World Lacrosse Championship. Most recently, Latch notched a tournament-best 43 points (26G, 17A) in the 2026 Asia-Pacific Sixes Lacrosse Championship. item.title: Hansi Flick admits ‘I’m trying to help Barcelona star regain his confidence’
item.description: Hansi Flick admits ‘I’m trying to help Barcelona star regain his confidence’ Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has admitted that he is currently working hard to help defender Alejandro Balde rediscover his best form. Left-back Balde has of course seen his name emerge as a prominent one in the media chatter surrounding Barcelona for several weeks now. Amid ongoing struggles for minutes in Catalunya’s capital, the 23-year-old has seen his Blaugrana future called into serious question. Balde, it has been murmured, could even be on the move as soon as January. Speaking during an appearance in front of the media on Monday, it therefore came as little surprise when the name of his struggling defender was put to the aforementioned Hansi Flick. And Barca’s headmaster made use of the opportunity to throw his backing behind Balde, assuring that he has not yet given up on the once so highly-regarded Spaniard: “I spoke to Balde and told him that this is normal. I have great respect for Balde, and I’m trying to help him regain his confidence. That’s what the coaching staff should do. He’s working hard to get back to his best, and I’m happy for him.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: What waiving Elliott Davison means for the Patriots
item.description: One day after their win over the Miami Dolphins, the New England Patriots decided to part ways with a member of their safety group. Elliott Davison, who had originally joined the 53-man roster from the practice squad in mid-October, was waived . Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots from a big-picture perspective. Unsurprising move When the Patriots announced their inactives on Sunday, the six-players list included four healthy scratches. Davison was one of them, reflecting his position near the bottom of the roster and the volatile status of his spot on the 53-man team. From that perspective alone, him getting the axe on Monday was no particular surprise — and that’s before putting injured reserve into consideration as well. After all, wide receiver Mack Hollins and fullback Reggie Gilliam are both eligible to return to practice and subsequently off IR this week, while offensive tackle Marcus Bryant’s 21-day window for activation is set to close on Wednesday. New England had no openings on its roster coming out of Week 8. It now has one, and it is likely to be used sooner rather than later. Safety shakeup The Patriots have had to deal with their fair share of depth questions across the roster this season, but the safety spot has been in relatively good shape. Led by team captain Kevin Byard and sophomore starter Craig Woodson, the group has enjoyed a level of stability others on the team can only dream of. Removing Davison from the equation does little to change that, given that he was the sixth option and played only 10 defensive snaps — all late during a blowout win over the Raiders in Week 5. 53-man roster (5): Kevin Byard III (31), Craig Woodson (4), Jaylen Reed (23), Brenden Schooler (41), Mike Brown (33) Injured reserve (1): Dell Pettus (24) The big question mark among the group is Dell Pettus, who remains on injured reserve despite being eligible to come back since Week 7. Should he be cleared for a return, he and Mike Brown might end up competing for one spot on the team as a backup/third safety and personal punt protector. Special teams impact Before being made inactive for the Dolphins game on Sunday, Davison saw most of his action on special teams. He played 57 combined snaps during his three active games, a share of 67% over that span. He lined up on kickoff coverage, kickoff return, punt return and field goal/extra point block — roles that were already redistributed versus Miami. From that point of view, his removal from the 53-man roster will not have a notable impact: he already had been replaced in that regard. Return possible An undrafted rookie in 2025, Davison will have to pass through the waiver wire before entering the open market. There is a theoretical chance that a team ends up putting in a claim on the 24-year-old to bring him aboard, but the expected outcome is that he won’t be picked up that way. item.title: Rams finally share good news about Myles Garrett
item.description: Myles Garrett will return to practice with the Los Angeles Rams this week, head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday. Garrett’s 21-day practice window will be opened at some point this week, meaning that the Rams have 21 days from then to either activate him to the 53-man roster or they will have to put him on IR for the rest of the season. If history is any indication, Garrett should be playing with the Rams again within three weeks, and probably sooner. Garrett has not suited up for L.A. since Week 1’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a knee injury. McVay also said that tight end Terrance Ferguson could return to practice this week also. Sean McVay says OLB Myles Garrett will practice this week and have that 21-day practice window opened. McVay also said TE Terrance Ferguson has a good chance to return to practice this week as well. — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) November 2, 2026 The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to the Cleveland Browns for Garrett in the offseason, but he has yet to record his first sack with L.A.. That could change as soon as this weekend’s game against the Washington Commanders. However, it wouldn’t be unexpected for the Rams to wait another week after that, or even until L.A. returns from a bye the week after. The good news is that after almost two months of waiting, Myles Garrett is almost finally back to the field.

item.title: Asa Newell’s $3.56 Million Option Shock For Hawks
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images The Atlanta Hawks just made a move that looks cheap on paper but carries a heavy price tag for the future. They exercised the third-year option on former first-round pick Asa Newell, locking in a salary of $3.56 million for the 2027-28 season. This decision keeps the 21-year-old big man under contract well past his rookie deal. Per Heavy.com , the team had to make this call by the November 2 deadline to secure his rights. It is a surprising financial commitment for a player who has barely cracked the rotation. Most fans expect teams to decline options on players who struggle for minutes. Newell has played just 47 games over two seasons, averaging 5.2 points and 2.2 rebounds in limited time. The Hawks are betting on a different path. According to Yahoo Sports , this was an easy decision because the deal remains a cheap option for a young player with talent. The organization sees potential where others might see a risk. They are paying for what Newell could become, not just what he is right now. A G League Dominance No One Saw Coming The real story here is not the NBA minutes. It is the numbers Newell put up in the G League. While he sat on the bench in Atlanta, he was tearing up the minor leagues. In 12 games with the College Park Skyhawks, he averaged a massive 22.8 points and 8.5 rebounds. Yardbarker reported that he also dished out 1.8 assists and blocked 1.6 shots per game. He looked like a star in the minors while struggling to find a spot in the big league rotation. This gap in performance is the key to understanding the Hawks’ logic. Newell showed he can guard and rebound at a high level when given the chance. He is 6-foot-10 and athletic, traits that coaches always crave. The Hawks believe his defensive versatility can help them shore up the frontcourt. According to Heavy.com, he is a flexible big man capable of guarding opponents while also hitting three-point shots at a respectable rate. That mix of size and skill is rare. The team thinks he can grow into a solid backup for Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu. A Crowded Frontcourt Creates a Tense Battle Here is the twist that makes this move even more interesting. The Hawks already have a crowded room of young big men. They drafted Zuby Ejiofor in the first round this past year, and Mouhamed Gueye is on the roster but currently injured. Yahoo Sports pointed out that all three players overlap in their skill sets. Keeping Newell means the team is committed to a logjam of forwards. They have to figure out who plays, who sits, and who gets traded. The decision also comes at a tough time for the franchise. The Hawks have lost four of their last five games and sit at a 3-4 record. item.title: When will the Golden State Valkyries parade be? Here's what to know
item.description: After Golden State Valkyries achieved an historic win, beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 Saturday night at Ballhalla, the team announced details of its championship parade! The Valkyries and the City of San Francisco will host the parade along the city's Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Here's what you need to know. What time will the parade start? Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay side of the Embarcadero. The parade will start at noon and is expected to end at 2 p.m. Where will the parade be? The parade will start at noon at the Ferry Building, travel along the Embarcadero, and end at King and 2nd streets. If I can't watch in person, how else can I watch? Viewers can watch TV coverage on ABC7, or stream the parade online on our website or the free ABC7 Bay Area mobile app starting at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. Who will be there? The team, coaches, staff and city leaders will all be there to celebrate the historic win. According to the Golden State Valkyries, Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, and city officials from across the Bay, are expected to be at the championship parade. Gabby Williams, who was named WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, will bang the GSV drum alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie to start the parade, the team said. Are there fan opportunities? Yes! Fan opportunities will include a viewing area, a championship merchandise truck, and various fan activation zones along the parade route. How will the weather be on Wednesday? It will be partly cloudy along the bay with temperatures in the upper 60s. item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 31: Malachi Tony #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates his touchdown with teammate Mark Fletcher Jr. #4 against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the first half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 31, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. The Miami Hurricanes led Nebraska 33-10 in the fourth quarter at Hard Rock Stadium in 2015. Nebraska stormed back to tie the game with a last-minute touchdown and two-point conversion. A Corn Elder pick and a walk off field goal delivered victory. I wrote about the game , saying there’s a W in “wrangle”. As in there was a fight but it ended with a win. This is from that piece: But here’s the thing – it didn’t. Miami won. Perhaps my disgust has subsided a great deal over the past week and a half….but the fact still remains. They…..won. And no one has ever complained about an undefeated team. Right now, that’s what Miami is. item.title: Former All-Pro Defender Not Sold on Steelers Winning AFC North
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy in a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sept. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers still have doubters as they sit atop the AFC North. The Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves in a very nice spot heading into their Week 9 bye. After defeating the Cleveland Browns 27-6 in Week 8, they now have sole possession of the AFC North at 6-2. Meanwhile, the Baltimore Ravens seem to have lost quarterback Lamar Jackson for the foreseeable future, and maybe even the rest of the season. However, former All-Pro safety Justin Simmons still doesn’t believe it will be the Steelers wearing the AFC North crown by the end of the regular season. “Give me the Cincinnati Bengals,” Simmons said on CBS Sports HQ . “Some people over here think the Pittsburgh Steelers are running off with the North. I’m not buying it. [The Bengals have] an improved defense. Before this game, they were league-best in sack differential. … Way improved for Joe Burrow. He’s not used to being this clean going into eight weeks into the season.” The Bengals do seem to be the Steelers biggest competitor to win the division, sitting in second place at 5-2. But Pittsburgh already handled business in its first meeting with Cincinnati in Week 3. That’s not to say the Steelers will sweep the Bengals this season, but they certainly have the momentum in their favor. Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson in a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sep. 29, 2026 — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now That answer is coming very soon, though. The Steelers are scheduled to face the Bengals for the second time when they come off their bye in Week 10. So, it’s safe to say Pittsburgh’s Week 9 bye is coming at the perfect time as it will not only give the team an opportunity to rest up for the second half of the season but also give it a little extra time to prepare for Cincinnati in a game that could have major playoff implications. The game is also fittingly scheduled to be played on Sunday Night Football with an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. item.title: Packers sign QB Cam Miller
item.description: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler is reporting that the Green Bay Packers have signed quarterback Cam Miller to their practice squad. The Packers had two openings on their practice squad coming into the week, so the team doesn’t need to make any corresponding roster move to execute this deal. With that being said, Green Bay already had one practice squad quarterback in Kedon Slovis, so there’s a possibility that his job moving forward is uncertain. Miller originally worked out for the Packers in early September, but the team continued to roll with Slovis at the time. Only one other quarterback, UFL MVP Jack Plummer, has worked out with Green Bay since the cutdown deadline . Cam Miller was drafted in round 6 pick 215 in the 2025 draft class. He scored a 6.08 #RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 412 out of 1048 QB from 1987 to 2025. https://t.co/DERSXGeq0I pic.twitter.com/iVLRMNbt7B — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 26, 2025 Miller was a sixth-round pick by the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025, and the former North Dakota State quarterback spent most of his rookie season on the practice squad. Late in the year, he was poached by the Miami Dolphins, where he spent training camp in 2026 before being released at the roster cutdown deadline. Beyond Miller’s September workout for the Packers, the Minnesota Vikings also kicked the tires on the quarterback about a month ago. In two pre-seasons, Miller has gone 36 of 75 passing for 373 yards, one touchdown, one interception and seven sacks. Here was The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s blurb on Miller as a draft prospect , when he was graded as a draftable prospect by the analyst: A four-year starter at North Dakota State, Miller was the point guard of former offensive coordinator Jake Landry’s run-heavy scheme (averaged just 21.9 pass attempts per game). A two-time FCS national champion as a starter (2022 and 2024), he set school records for career passing yards (9,720), completions (759) and total offense (11,997). Miller is an intelligent game manager who takes what the defense gives him and relies on timing and placement over pure arm power. The son of a football coach, his mental approach and on-field production showed improvements each season, although he will continue to have his doubters because of the level of competition he faced. Overall, Miller won’t wow you right away because the physical traits are average. The more you watch, though, the more you come to appreciate his decision-making and feel for the position. He can be an asset in an NFL quarterback room as a reserve. Instead, the talk surrounding the running back after the game was about one of his celebrations. Jacobs was recently removed from the commissioner’s exempt list after getting arrested for domestic violence, for which he reached a plea deal to avoid jail time. item.title: Brewers extend qualifying offer to Jake Bauers; 5 become free agents
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are putting their money where their mouth is regarding one of their key players from the World Series run. The team extended a one-year qualifying offer of $23.15 million to first baseman Jake Bauers, the National League Championship Series MVP , as part of a flurry of moves ahead of free agency officially beginning at 4 p.m. Nov. 2. Bauers has until Nov. 17 to either accept or reject the Brewers' offer. Coming off a breakout year in which he had an .874 OPS and slugged 26 homers for the World Series champions, there will be ample interest in Bauers for far more than the price tag of the qualifying offer. But Bauers, an integral piece of the clubhouse who came to greatly appreciate playing in Milwaukee, could get more in 2027 alone on the qualifying offer than as a free agent. While Bauers is not yet technically a free agent, catcher Gary Sánchez and pitchers Antonio Senzatela and Dustin May are after their mutual options were not exercised. The Brewers declined the options on Sánchez and Senzatela, while May turned down his $20 million option. Pitchers Bryse Wilson and Jared Koenig also became free agents after clearing waivers and electing free agency. Wilson will become a minor-league free agent. Outfielder Akil Baddoo, who spent the entire season at Class AAA Nashville, was claimed off waivers by the Pittsburgh Pirates to round out the club's moves. The Brewers' 40-man roster now stands at 33 players. This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Brewers extend qualifying offer to Jake Bauers; 5 become free agents

item.description: Following a painful collapse from the Florida State Seminoles ‘ perfect 13-0 season in 2023, fans reached a breaking point. Deep frustration with the program’s sharp decline turned every week into a high-stakes test for the leadership in Tallahassee. But what was meant to be a serious statement high above the stadium took an unexpected turn. After the game, analyst Shan Shariff did not mince words about Schottenheimer’s competence for the Cowboys job. Brian Schottenheimer Comes Under Fire After Cowboys’ Week 8 Loss During Monday’s segment of “Shan and RJ,” Shariff gave a scathing assessment of Schottenheimer’s Cowboys’ reign. “Brian Schottenheimer is so in over his head; he’s drowning, and he’s reaching out for Christian to kind of doggy paddle,” Shariff said. “Well, Christian’s got two cinder blocks tied around his damn legs as well. You have a coach and a coordinator that the Joneses grossly overestimated in terms of lack of experience.” Dallas held double-digit leads multiple times against the Cardinals but couldn’t put the game away. The Cowboys allowed Arizona quarterback Gardner Minshew to throw two touchdowns in the final 2:16 of regulation, including the game-tying score with six seconds left, before Arizona ultimately won on a field goal in overtime.
